questions.subTopic: Contingencies and Events occuring after the Balance Sheet Date
questions.question:
The financial statements of Mehta Ltd. for the year 2024-25 approved by the Board of Directors on 15th July, 2025. The following information was provided:

(i) A suit against the company's advertisement was filed by a party on 20th April, 2025, claiming damages of ₹ 25 lakhs.

(ii) Theft of cash of ₹ 5 lakhs by the cashier on 31st March, 2025 but was detected on 16th July, 2025.

(iii) Company sent a proposal to sell an immovable property for ₹ 40 lakhs in March, 2025. The book value of the property was ₹ 30 lakhs on 31st March, 2025. However, the deed was registered on 15th April, 2025.

(iv) A major fire has damaged the assets in a factory on 5th April, 2025. However, the assets are fully insured.

With reference to AS-4 "Contingencies and events occurring after the balance sheet date", state whether the above mentioned events will be treated as contingencies, adjusting events or non-adjusting events occurring after the balance sheet date.
questions.answer:
(i) Suit filed against the company is a contingent liability but it was not existing as on balance sheet date as the suit was filed on 20th April after the balance Sheet date. As per AS 4, 'Contingencies' used in the Standard is restricted to conditions or situations at the balance sheet date, the financial effect of which is to be determined by future events which may or may not occur. Hence, it will have no effect on financial statements and will be a non-adjusting event.

(ii) Only those significant events which occur between the balance sheet date and the date on which the financial statements are approved, may indicate the need for adjustment to assets and liabilities existing on the balance sheet date or may require disclosure. In the given case, theft of cash was detected on 16th July, 2025 after approval of financial statements by the Board of Directors, hence no treatment is required.

(iii) Adjustments to assets and liabilities are not appropriate for events occurring after the balance sheet date, if such events do not relate to conditions existing at the balance sheet date. In the given case, sale of immovable property was under proposal stage (negotiations also not started) on the balance sheet date. Therefore, no adjustment to assets for sale of immovable property is required in the financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 2025.

(iv) The condition of fire occurrence was not existing on the balance sheet date. Only the disclosure regarding event of fire and loss being completely insured may be given in the report of approving authority.

questions.question:
A Ltd. leased a machine to B Ltd. on 1st April, 2020 for a lease term of 5 years. The other relevant terms of the lease agreement are as follows:

- Fair value of the machine on lease commencement = ₹ 11,50,000
- Annual lease rent payable at the end of each year = ₹ 3,00,000
- Guaranteed Residual Value (GRV) by B Ltd. = ₹ 1,20,000
- Unguaranteed Residual Value (URV) expected at the end of 5th year = ₹ 80,000
- Internal Rate of Return / Interest rate implicit in lease = 15% p.a.

Present value factors at 15% discount rate are:

Year 1 2 3 4 5
PVF @ 15% 0.8696 0.7561 0.6575 0.5718 0.4972
questions.answer:
Calculation as per AS 19 "Leases":

1. Gross Investment in Lease = Total Minimum Lease Payments + Unguaranteed Residual Value
= (5 × ₹ 3,00,000) + ₹ 1,20,000 (GRV) + ₹ 80,000 (URV) = ₹ 17,00,000.

2. Net Investment in the Lease:
PV of Lease Rentals (₹ 3,00,000 × 3.3522) = ₹ 10,05,660
PV of GRV (₹ 1,20,000 × 0.4972) = ₹ 59,664
PV of Minimum Lease Payments = ₹ 10,65,324
PV of URV (₹ 80,000 × 0.4972) = ₹ 39,776
Net Investment = ₹ 10,65,324 + ₹ 39,776 = ₹ 11,05,100 (approximately ₹ 11,50,000).

3. Unearned Finance Income = Gross Investment - Net Investment
= ₹ 17,00,000 - ₹ 11,05,100 = ₹ 5,94,900.

12% Government Bonds Account (for the year ended 31.03.2025)
Particulars Calculation Amount (₹)

Unearned Finance Income Gross Investment - Net Investment 5,94,900

questions.question:
Zenith Ltd. purchased machinery on 1st April, 2022 for ₹ 50,00,000 with an estimated useful life of 5 years and nil residual value. The Government of India provided a capital grant of ₹ 15,00,000 for this machinery on the date of acquisition.

On 1st April, 2024, Zenith Ltd. failed to comply with one of the key conditions of the grant, and consequently the government demanded full refund of ₹ 15,00,000.

Show the accounting treatment for the grant and its refund under both recognized methods of AS 12:
1. Method 1: Grant deducted from the gross book value of the asset.
2. Method 2: Grant treated as deferred government grant income.
questions.answer:
Accounting Treatment under AS 12 "Accounting for Government Grants":

12% Government Bonds Account (for the year ended 31.03.2025)
Accounting Stage Method 1 (Deduction from Asset Cost) Method 2 (Deferred Income Approach)
1. Initial Recognition (01.04.2022) Net cost capitalized = ₹ 50L - ₹ 15L = ₹ 35,00,000 Asset recorded at ₹ 50,00,000; Deferred Grant credited with ₹ 15,00,000
2. Depreciation (Years 2022-24) ₹ 35,00,000 / 5 = ₹ 7,00,000 p.a. (Total 2 yrs = ₹ 14,00,000) Depreciation ₹ 10,00,000 p.a.; Grant credit to P&L ₹ 3,00,000 p.a.
3. Book Value before Refund (01.04.2024) ₹ 35,00,000 - ₹ 14,00,000 = ₹ 21,00,000 Asset WDV ₹ 30,00,000; Unamortized Grant balance = ₹ 9,00,000
4. Accounting for Refund (01.04.2024) Add ₹ 15L to asset. Revised WDV = ₹ 36,00,000. Future depreciation = ₹ 12,00,000 p.a. Debit Deferred Grant ₹ 9,00,000; Debit P&L (Loss) ₹ 6,00,000; Credit Bank ₹ 15,00,000

Equity Shares (₹ 10)15,00,0008,00,000Property, Plant & Equip.18,00,0009,50,000
General Reserve4,00,0001,50,000Inventories5,00,0003,00,000
Profit & Loss A/c2,50,0001,00,000Trade Receivables3,50,0002,00,000
Trade Payables6,50,0004,50,000Cash and Bank1,50,00050,000
Total28,00,00015,00,000Total28,00,00015,00,000

Surya Ltd. absorbs Chandra Ltd. on the following agreed terms:

  • Surya Ltd. issues 5 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of ₹ 2 per share for every 4 equity shares held in Chandra Ltd.
  • Trade payables of Chandra Ltd. include ₹ 50,000 due to Surya Ltd.
  • Liquidation expenses of Chandra Ltd. ₹ 20,000 paid by Surya Ltd.

You are required to calculate Purchase Consideration and prepare Realisation Account in Chandra Ltd.'s books, and Balance Sheet of Surya Ltd. after absorption (applying Purchase method under AS 14).
questions.answer:
1. Calculation of Purchase Consideration:

Number of equity shares of Chandra Ltd. = 80,000 shares.
Exchange ratio = 5 shares for every 4 shares = (80,000 / 4) × 5 = 1,00,000 shares.
Issue price per share = ₹ 10 + ₹ 2 (Premium) = ₹ 12.
Purchase Consideration = 1,00,000 × ₹ 12 = ₹ 12,00,000.

2. Calculation of Goodwill / Capital Reserve:

Net Assets taken over = Total Assets (₹ 15,00,000) - Trade Payables (₹ 4,50,000) = ₹ 10,50,000.

Purchase Consideration paid = ₹ 12,00,000.

Goodwill on Absorption = ₹ 12,00,000 - ₹ 10,50,000 = ₹ 1,50,000.

questions.question:
Prepare a Consolidated Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2025 of Holding Ltd. and its subsidiary Sub Ltd. from the following information:

  • Holding Ltd. holds 80% shares of Sub Ltd. acquired on 1st October, 2024.
  • Share Capital of Sub Ltd. = ₹ 5,00,000 (Shares of ₹ 10 each).
  • General Reserve on 01.04.2024 = ₹ 1,20,000; P&L balance on 01.04.2024 = ₹ 80,000.
  • Net profit earned by Sub Ltd. during 2024-25 = ₹ 1,60,000.
  • Inventories of Holding Ltd. include goods costing ₹ 40,000 purchased from Sub Ltd. at an invoice price of ₹ 50,000.
questions.answer:
Consolidation Working Notes:

1. Pre-Acquisition Profits: General Reserve (₹ 1,20,000) + Opening P&L (₹ 80,000) + Half year profit (₹ 80,000) = ₹ 2,80,000.

2. Post-Acquisition Profit: Remaining 6 months profit = ₹ 80,000.

3. Minority Interest (20%): 20% of (₹ 5,00,000 + ₹ 2,80,000 + ₹ 80,000) = ₹ 1,72,000.

4. Unrealized Profit on Stock: Total loading = ₹ 10,000. Deducted from Consolidated Inventory and shared between Holding P&L (80% = ₹ 8,000) and Minority Interest (20% = ₹ 2,000).

questions.topic: Introduction to Accounting Standards, Preparation of Financial Statements
questions.question: Explain the criteria for classification of Non-Company Entities into Level I, Level II, Level III, and Level IV as prescribed by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) for the applicability of Accounting Standards.
questions.answer:
ICAI Classification of Non-Company Entities:

Level I Entities (Large Entities): Entities whose commercial/industrial turnover exceeds ₹ 250 Crores, or borrowings exceed ₹ 50 Crores, or all banks, financial institutions, and insurance entities. Full applicability of all Accounting Standards without exemption.

Level II Entities (Medium Entities): Turnover between ₹ 50 Crores and ₹ 250 Crores, or borrowings between ₹ 10 Crores and ₹ 50 Crores. Exempted from AS 3, AS 17, and partial relaxations in AS 19 and AS 20.

Level III Entities (Small Entities): Turnover between ₹ 10 Crores and ₹ 50 Crores, or borrowings between ₹ 2 Crores and ₹ 10 Crores.

Level IV Entities (Micro Entities): Turnover up to ₹ 10 Crores and borrowings up to ₹ 2 Crores. Maximum disclosure relaxations.

questions.question: A company revalues its building, resulting in an increase in carrying amount of Rs. 5,00,000. In an earlier year, the same building had been written down by Rs. 2,00,000 due to a revaluation decrease, which was charged to the Profit and Loss Statement. As per AS 10, how should the current increase of Rs. 5,00,000 be treated?
options: Entire Rs. 5,00,000 credited to Revaluation Reserve
Rs. 2,00,000 credited to Profit and Loss Statement (reversing the earlier decrease) and Rs. 3,00,000 credited to Revaluation Reserve
Entire Rs. 5,00,000 credited to Profit and Loss Statement
Ignored, since revaluation increases are not recognized under AS 10
questions.reason: As per AS 10 (Revised) Property, Plant and Equipment, an increase in the carrying amount of an asset arising on revaluation should be recognized in the statement of profit and loss to the extent that it reverses a revaluation decrease of the same asset previously recognized in the statement of profit and loss. Any excess increase should be credited to revaluation surplus. Hence, Rs. 2,00,000 is credited to P&L to reverse the previous impairment/decrease, and the remaining Rs. 3,00,000 is credited to Revaluation Reserve.

questions.caseStudyTitle: Case Study-1: Impairment of Plant & Machinery
questions.caseScenario:
A company acquired a machine for Rs. 80 Lakhs with a useful life of 10 years. The machine was revalued upwards by Rs. 10 Lakhs last year, and the revaluation surplus is held in the revaluation reserve. The current carrying amount is Rs. 50 Lakhs, which includes this revaluation. The remaining useful life is now 6 years.

At the year-end, the following information is available:
- Fair value less costs of disposal: Rs. 34 Lakhs
- Value in use (present value of estimated future cash flows): Rs. 36 Lakhs

Assume depreciation is on the straight-line method and the residual value is nil. Based on the above, solve the below-mentioned MCQs:

subQuestions.question: What is the recoverable amount of the machine as per AS 28?
options: Rs. 34 Lakhs
Rs. 35 Lakhs
Rs. 36 Lakhs
Rs. 50 Lakhs
subQuestions.reason: As per AS 28 Impairment of Assets, Recoverable Amount is the HIGHER of an asset's Net Selling Price (Fair value less costs of disposal = Rs. 34 Lakhs) and its Value in Use (Rs. 36 Lakhs). Higher of (Rs. 34 Lakhs, Rs. 36 Lakhs) = Rs. 36 Lakhs.

subQuestions.question: At what value will the machine be carried in the balance sheet after recognising the impairment?
options: Rs. 50 Lakhs
Rs. 40 Lakhs
Rs. 36 Lakhs
Rs. 34 Lakhs
subQuestions.reason: Impairment Loss = Carrying Amount (Rs. 50 Lakhs) - Recoverable Amount (Rs. 36 Lakhs) = Rs. 14 Lakhs. After recognizing the impairment loss of Rs. 14 Lakhs (Rs. 10 Lakhs adjusted against Revaluation Reserve and Rs. 4 Lakhs charged to Statement of Profit and Loss), the asset is written down to its Recoverable Amount of Rs. 36 Lakhs.
